Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 28, verse 1:

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Tafsir of Surat al-Qasas

It is Makkiyya (revealed in Makkah), except for the words of the Exalted: ﴿Those to whom We have given the Book﴾ up to His words: ﴿We do not seek the ignorant﴾.

In this surah there is a verse that is neither Makkan nor Madinan, and it is the words of the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, He who has imposed upon you the Qur'an will surely return you to a place of return﴾. This verse was revealed between Makkah and Madinah, while the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was at al-Juhfah, which is one of the stations (manazil), and that was when the Prophet (ﷺ) migrated from Makkah to Madinah.

The words of the Exalted: ﴿Ta-Sin-Mim﴾. Qatadah said: it is one of the names of the Qur'an. It is related from al-Hasan that he said: it is one of the names of the surah. It is related from Ibn 'Abbas, in one narration, that he said: it is the Greatest Name of Allah. And we have explained other than this.

And His saying: ﴿These are the verses of the Clear Book﴾. It is said: *bāna* and *abāna* have the same meaning, and likewise the expression *bayyantu al-shay'* and *ubayyinuhu* (I made the thing clear). Al-Zajjaj said: "*al-Mubīn* means that it makes clear the lawful from the unlawful, and the truth from falsehood."

God's words: ﴿We recite to you some of the news of Moses and Pharaoh in truth﴾ means: in truth (bil-haqq), that is, with sincerity (bil-sidq).

And His words: ﴿for a people who believe﴾ mean: who affirm (yusaddiqun). And "naba' (news)" is a name for information (khabar).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 28, verse 4:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, Pharaoh exalted himself in the land﴾, meaning: he became arrogant and tyrannical. It is also said: he transgressed and subjugated. "The land" is the land of Egypt. ﴿And made its people into factions﴾, meaning: groups.

His saying, glorified and exalted is He: ﴿He oppressed a faction among them﴾. What is meant by the "faction" is the Children of Israel. The explanation of the oppression is what is mentioned afterwards, which is His saying: ﴿slaughtering their sons and keeping their women alive﴾. It is recited in the irregular (shadh) reading: "yudhabbiḥu abnāahum" without the doubling (tashdid). This is called oppression because they were unable and too weak to repel this from themselves. Wahb ibn Munabbih and others mentioned that Pharaoh saw in his sleep as if a fire had come out from the direction of al-Sham until it surrounded Egypt and burned the Copts while leaving the Children of Israel. When he woke in the morning, he summoned the soothsayers (kahana) and informed them of his dream. They said: a man from the Children of Israel will emerge, and your destruction and the destruction of the Copts will be at his hand. Some of them narrated that they said: a boy will be born. Thereupon Pharaoh ordered the slaughter of the male children of the Children of Israel and the sparing of their females. Al-Zajjaj said: this was from his foolishness, for if the soothsayers were truthful, killing would be of no use, and if they were lying, there is also no point in killing. Wahb said: when they did this to the boys of the Children of Israel, death quickly came upon their elders. The notables of the Copts gathered before Pharaoh and said to him: you are killing the sons of the Children of Israel, and death has quickly come upon their elders, so soon none of them will remain, and the work will return to us. They had been employing the Children of Israel in hard labour.

Al-Suddi, regarding His saying ﴿and made its people into factions﴾, said: they had divided the Children of Israel into groups: one group would build, another group would plough and sow, another group would plant, another group would tend the animals, and similar kinds of work. Whoever could not perform any work was made to pay the jizya. When Pharaoh heard their words, he ordered that the boys be killed for one year and spared for one year. Thus Aaron, peace be upon him, was born in the year in which the boys were not killed, and Moses was born in the year in which the boys were killed.

His saying: ﴿Indeed, he was among the corrupters﴾, meaning: in the land.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 28, verse 5:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And We wished to bestow favour﴾, i.e., to bestow blessings.

And His saying: ﴿upon those who were deemed weak in the land﴾, i.e., the Children of Israel.

And His saying: ﴿and make them leaders﴾, i.e., rulers (wulat).

And His saying: ﴿and make them the inheritors﴾, i.e., the inheritors of the kingdom of Pharaoh and the Copts. It has been narrated that when God drowned Pharaoh, the Children of Israel returned to Egypt and enslaved those of the Copts who remained.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And We will establish them in the land﴾, meaning: We will make for them a settled land (miṣr) in which they may dwell.

And His saying: ﴿and We will show Pharaoh and Haman and their hosts from them that which they were fearing﴾. Al-ḥadhar (caution) is guarding oneself against harm.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 28, verse 7:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And We revealed to the mother of Musa﴾. In the narrative: when the mother of Musa became pregnant with Musa, the pregnancy did not show on her as it shows on women, and she gave birth without anyone knowing of her delivery. She began to nurse him in secret. Then she feared that people would notice him and he would be slaughtered. So God, may He be exalted, cast into her heart what He mentions in this verse.

Revelation (wahy) is informing in secret. Most of the exegetes hold that the meaning of His saying ﴿And We revealed to the mother of Musa﴾ is her inspiration (ilham), that this meaning was placed in her heart. Some of them said: she saw that in a dream. Others said: it is revelation in the true sense, and an angel came to her with this from God, except that she was not a prophetess.

His saying ﴿that suckle him﴾: opinions differ regarding the duration of nursing. Some said eight months, some said four months, and some said three months.

His saying ﴿And when you fear for him, then cast him into the river﴾: the fear for him is the fear of slaughter.

His saying ﴿then cast him into the river﴾: al-yamm (yam) means the sea, and what is meant here, according to the view of all the exegetes, is the Nile. Ibn 'Abbas said: she summoned a carpenter and had a chest (tabut) made. That carpenter went and informed Pharaoh, and he came with helpers, and God obliterated his eyes so that he could not find anything. Then he made a covenant with God that if He restored his sight to him, he would turn the helpers away from him. God restored his sight to him, and he turned the helpers away. Afterwards he believed in Musa, peace be upon him, and he was the Believer of the family of Pharaoh (Mu'min Al Fir'awn), and his name was Hizqil.

His saying ﴿And do not fear and do not grieve﴾: that is, do not fear for him from drowning. It was said: from being lost. His saying ﴿and do not grieve﴾: that is, do not grieve over separation from him.

His saying ﴿Indeed, We will return him to you and make him among the messengers﴾: its meaning is apparent. The verse contains two commands, two prohibitions, two reports, and two glad tidings. As for the two commands: His saying ﴿that suckle him﴾ and His saying ﴿then cast him into the river﴾. As for the two prohibitions: His saying ﴿And do not fear and do not grieve﴾. As for the two reports: His saying ﴿And We revealed to the mother of Musa﴾, and likewise His saying ﴿And when you fear for him﴾. As for the two glad tidings: His saying, may He be exalted, ﴿Indeed, We will return him to you and make him among the messengers﴾. The verse is counted among the eloquent passages of the Qur'an.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 28, verse 8:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Then the family of Pharaoh picked him up﴾ (al-iltiqat) is the finding of a thing without seeking it. As for the narrative: his mother placed Musa in a chest, came to it and cast it into the Nile. The water carried it to the side of Pharaoh's house. The maidservants had gone out to draw water, and the water returned the chest to the watering place from which they drew. It is also said: the chest caught on the tree that was there. Musa, in Hebrew, is Musha: "mu" is water, and "sha" is tree. He was named Musha because he was found between the water and the tree. The maidservants took the chest and went with it to the wife of Pharaoh, who was Asiya bint Muzahim. It is said that she was from the Children of Israel, and that Pharaoh had married her from among them.

And His saying: ﴿That it might be for them an enemy and a grief﴾ (this lam is the lam of consequence, and it is said: the lam of becoming, for they did not pick him up so that he would become for them an enemy and a grief, but their affair came to this outcome, so the lam is mentioned in the sense of becoming). This is like the saying of the poet:

(Our wealth we gather for the heirs of inheritance... and our houses we build for the ruin of time.)

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, Pharaoh and Haman and their hosts were sinners﴾ means: abandoning the path of truth.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 28, verse 9:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And the wife of Pharaoh said, "A comfort of the eye for me and for you."﴾ Regarding the report: the wife of Pharaoh carried the child to Pharaoh and said, "A comfort of the eye for me and for you." Pharaoh said, "A comfort of the eye for you, but as for me, no." And in this report it is narrated that the Prophet said: "If Pharaoh had said, 'A comfort of the eye for me,' Allah would have guided him just as He guided his wife." And the report is gharib (unusual, weakly transmitted).

And in some tafsir works: Pharaoh intended to kill him, and said, "Perhaps he is one of the enemies." So his wife asked him to spare the child, and he granted her request.

And His saying: ﴿Do not kill him; perhaps he will benefit us, or we may adopt him as a son.﴾ It is narrated that Asiya had no child, and it was said that her children used to die, so she said, "Or we may adopt him as a son" for this reason.

And His saying: ﴿while they perceive not﴾ means: they do not know the reality of the matter.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 28, verse 10:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And the heart of the mother of Musa became empty﴾. It has been said: "wa-asbaha" means "sara" (became), and it has also been said that it is in its literal sense, and its usage in this place is figurative (majaz). Its meaning is: the mother of Musa and her heart became empty (farighan).

Scholars differ regarding His saying ﴿farighan﴾ (empty). The majority hold that what is meant by it is empty of everything except the remembrance of Musa and grief over him. This is the view of Ibn Mas'ud, Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, Qatadah, al-Dahhak and others.

The second view is that His saying ﴿farighan﴾ means free from grief over him, because of her knowledge of the truth of Allah's promise. This is the view of Abu 'Ubaydah. Al-Qutaybi and others rejected this view, saying: "How can this be valid when Allah, may He be exalted, says: ﴿Indeed, she was about to reveal him, had We not fortified her heart﴾?"

The third view is that "farighan" means forgetful of the revelation that was sent down to her and of the covenant taken from her, that she should not grieve because of the severity of the trial concerning him. This is the meaning of the saying of al-Hasan. In the irregular (shadhdh) reading it is recited as "faza'an" (fearful). We have already explained that the meaning of His saying ﴿fa-asbaha﴾ is "sara" (became), and they cited poetry in this regard:

(The caliphs passed away with the rightly-guided affair... and blame became attached to al-Walid.)

His saying ﴿she was about to reveal him﴾: Ibn 'Abbas said: she was about to say: "O my son!"

His saying ﴿had We not fortified her heart﴾: that is, with patience. It has been said: with belief in the promise, and it has been said: with divine protection (al-'ismah).

His saying ﴿so that she would be among the believers﴾: that is, among those who affirm the truth.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 28, verse 11:

As for the words of Allah the Exalted, ﴿And she said to his sister, "Follow him."﴾ In the narration, the name of the sister was Maryam. His words, ﴿Follow him﴾ mean: follow his trail (qassa, to trace or track), and from this comes the word al-qasas (narrative), because it is a report in which one part follows another.

His words, ﴿and she watched him from afar﴾ mean: from a distance. It was also said: from the side (ʿan janb). In the narration, she was walking alongside and looking furtively, while letting the people think that she was not looking.

His words, ﴿while they did not perceive﴾ mean: they did not perceive that their destruction would come at the hand of Musa (Moses). It was also said: they did not know that the infant was Musa, and that the one searching for him was his mother and his sister. They cited the poet's words, using ʿan janb in the sense of "from a distance": (So do not ask me for a gift from afar, for a man who is in the midst of the tents is a stranger.)

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 28, verse 12:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And We had forbidden him the wet-nurses before that﴾. That is: We prevented him from accepting suckling. The intended meaning of "forbidding" here is not the legal prohibition (al-tahrim al-shar'i); rather, the intended meaning is prevention (al-man'). Imru' al-Qays said in verse:

(She moved about to throw me down, so I said to her: "Desist! I am a man whose being thrown down is forbidden to you.")

That is: prevented. In the narrative: Musa remained for eight nights, not accepting any breast, crying out, while they were searching for a wet-nurse for him.

His saying: ﴿She said: "Shall I direct you"﴾, meaning: the sister of Musa said: "Shall I direct you ﴿to a household who will rear him for you?﴾"

His saying: ﴿and they will be sincere to him﴾, that is: they will be compassionate toward him. Sincerity (al-nush) is the opposite of deceit (al-ghish). It has also been said: sincerity is purifying the deed from the impurities of corruption. From this is his saying: "Indeed, religion is sincerity." It was asked: "To whom?" He said: "To Allah, to His Messenger, to His Book, and to the Muslims." The report is established; it was narrated by Tamim al-Dari.

In the narrative: the people of Pharaoh grew suspicious of the words of Musa's sister and said: "You know him, otherwise what is the meaning of your sincerity toward him?" So Allah inspired her, until she said: "I said this out of desire for the pleasure of the king and our connection with him." It is also reported that when Musa's mother was brought, and he found her scent, he leapt toward her breast and began to suckle it until his sides were filled with satisfaction. Al-Suddi said: they used to give her a dinar every day.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 28, verse 13:

And His saying: ﴿So We returned him to his mother, that her eye might be comforted and she would not grieve﴾, meaning: that her eye might be comforted by Musa's return to her, and ﴿she would not grieve﴾, meaning: and so that she would not grieve.

And His saying: ﴿and that she might know that the promise of Allah is true﴾, because He had promised her that He would return him to her.

And His saying: ﴿but most of them do not know﴾, meaning: they do not know that the promise of Allah is true.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 28, verse 14:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And when he reached his full strength (ashuddah)﴾. Ibn ʿAbbas said: al-ashudd is thirty years. It is related from Sufyan al-Thawri that it is thirty-four years. It was also said: thirty-three years, and it was said: twenty-five years, and it was said: twenty years, and it was said: [eighteen] years.

His words: ﴿and was firmly established (istawa)﴾. Ibn ʿAbbas said: forty years. It is related from others: ﴿istawa﴾ means that his youth reached its end.

His words: ﴿We gave him judgment and knowledge﴾, meaning: understanding (al-fiqh), intellect (al-ʿaql) and knowledge (al-ʿilm).

His words: ﴿Thus do We reward the good-doers﴾, the meaning is clear.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 28, verse 15:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And he entered the city﴾. In the tafsir: the city was the city of ʿAyn Shams (Heliopolis). It was also said: the city of Memphis (Manf). On the authority of al-Suddi, who said: Musa used to ride in Pharaoh's vehicles and wear his clothing, and he was called "the son of Pharaoh." Once Pharaoh rode out with his retinue (ḥashm) to some of the cities, and Musa was absent. He returned after Pharaoh had ridden out, so he rode in pursuit of him, and he reached the city at the time of the midday rest (al-qā'ila), when the people were occupied with the midday rest. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿and he entered the city at a time of unawareness on the part of its people﴾, that is, they were heedless of the remembrance of Musa.

And His saying: ﴿and he found in it two men fighting﴾. In the narrative: he found a Copt (qibṭī) forcing an Israelite (isrāʾīlī) to carry firewood to the kitchen of Pharaoh. His saying: ﴿fighting﴾ means: disputing and contending. His saying: ﴿one of his own faction and the other of his enemy﴾, that is: the Israelite was of his faction and the Copt was of his enemy. The Children of Israel had been informed about Musa's whereabouts, since they knew that he was one of them. It is also said: ﴿one of his own faction and the other of his enemy﴾ means: this one is a believer and this one is an unbeliever.

And His saying: ﴿So the one who was of his faction asked him for help﴾. Istighāthah (al-istighātha) means seeking assistance (ṭalab al-maʿūna). And His saying: ﴿so Musa struck him﴾. Ibn Masʿūd recited: "fa-lakazahu Mūsā" (فلكزه موسى). Al-lakz and al-wakz are one and the same, and they mean striking with the gathered palm (jamʿ al-kaff). It was also said that al-wakz is striking in the chest, and al-lakz is striking in the back. In some of the exegeses: Musa closed his fist (ʿaqada thalāthan wa-thamānīna) and struck him a blow with it in his chest, and he was very strong, so he killed the man. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿and he dispatched him﴾, that is, he killed him. It is said: Fulan "qaḍā" means he died. If it is asked: how is this permissible for Musa? We say: he did not intend to kill, rather the killing occurred by mistake, and his intention was to rescue the Israelite from his oppression.

And His saying: ﴿He said: This is of the work of Satan﴾, that is, of his adornment. And His saying: ﴿Indeed, he is a manifest, misleading enemy﴾, that is, misleading in clear error.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 28, verse 16:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿He said, "My Lord, I have wronged myself, so forgive me"﴾, meaning: by killing the Copt without His command. ﴿So He forgave him﴾, that is: so forgive me for what I have done.

And His saying: ﴿So He forgave him. Indeed, He is the Forgiving, the Merciful﴾, that is: God forgave him, for indeed God is Forgiving and Merciful.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 28, verse 17:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿He said, "My Lord, by that which You have bestowed upon me"﴾ — i.e., You have bestowed favor upon me by forgiveness.

And His saying: ﴿So never will I be a supporter of the criminals﴾ — i.e., a helper of the criminals. In some tafsirs it is stated that His saying ﴿So never will I be a supporter of the criminals﴾ was a slip (zallah) from Musa when he did not attach to it the will of Allah or seeking help from Allah. A person rarely says this statement and utters it in this unrestricted manner without being tested, so Musa was tested on the second day with what Allah the Exalted mentioned, namely His saying, the Exalted:

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 28, verse 18:

﴿So he became in the city, fearful and watchful.﴾ Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: he kept looking about [him]. It is also said: he was awaiting pursuit. In the narration (al-qissa): when Musa killed that man, no one had seen him, and he buried him in the sand. It is narrated that his people found him slain, so they came to Pharaoh and mentioned that to him. He said: "Seek his killer so that I may exact retaliation (qisas) from him for it." So they began searching for him, while Musa was afraid.

As for His words: ﴿Then behold, the one who had sought his help the day before was calling him for help.﴾ That is, he was crying out to him for help and shouting to him from afar. That Israelite had been pressed into forced labour by another Egyptian, and Musa saw him and asked him for assistance.

As for His words: ﴿Musa said to him, "Indeed, you are clearly a misguided one."﴾ The majority hold that Musa said this to the Israelite, for he had led him astray the day before, meaning: he had caused him to fall into error. So the meaning of His words ﴿ghawin﴾ ("misguided") is: one who causes others to fall into error.

As for His words: ﴿mubin﴾ ("clear"), that means: evident. It is also said that he said this to the Egyptian, but the more correct view is the first.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 28, verse 19:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿So when he intended to strike the one who was an enemy to both of them﴾. In the exegesis: Musa was overcome by tenderness and mercy toward the Israelite, so he intended to strike the Copt. The Israelite thought that he wanted to strike him, because Musa had said to him: "Indeed, you are clearly a misguided man."

And His saying: ﴿He said, "O Musa, do you intend to kill me as you killed a person yesterday? You intend only to be a tyrant in the land"﴾, meaning: the Israelite said, ﴿as you killed a person yesterday, you intend only﴾, i.e., you intend nothing ﴿except to be a tyrant in the land﴾, i.e., you kill in anger, and whoever kills in anger is a tyrant (jabbar). It is also said: whoever kills two souls without right is among the tyrants of the earth.

And His saying: ﴿and you do not intend to be among the reformers﴾, i.e., among those who bring about peace between people. In the narration: when the Israelite said this and the Copt heard it, he realized that the one who had been killed yesterday had in fact been killed by Musa. So he went to Pharaoh and mentioned that to him, and Pharaoh sent out to seek Musa in order to kill him for it.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 28, verse 20:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And there came a man from the farthest part of the city, running﴾. It is said: his name was Shamʿun, and it is said: Shamʿan. And it was said: he was Ḥizqil (Ezekiel), a believer from the family of Pharaoh.

And His saying: ﴿"O Moses, the chiefs are conferring about you, to kill you"﴾. That is, they are consulting about killing you. It was also said: some of them command others to kill you. And it was said: Pharaoh said, "Wherever you find him, kill him."

And His saying: ﴿"So leave; indeed I am to you among the sincere advisers"﴾. That is, sincere advisers to you regarding the matter of departing. Naṣīḥah (sincere counsel) toward a person is pointing out to him what will set his affairs right, and the early generation (al-salaf) used to seek this from one another. Abū Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, said when he delivered a sermon: "If I do well, then assist me, and if I go astray, then set me right." It is narrated that a man said to ʿUmar: "Fear Allah, O ʿUmar," and some of the people denounced him for it, but ʿUmar said: "Leave him; we will not cease to be good so long as such things are said to us." And it is related from one of them that he was asked: "Do you want to give counsel?" He said: "In private, yes; in public, no."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 28, verse 21:

His saying: ﴿So he went out from it, fearful, watching lest he be pursued﴾. That is: awaiting pursuit. In the narrative, Pharaoh sent (men) to seek him when he was informed of his flight, and said: "Ride the mountain paths, for he does not know how the road goes."

It is also related that he went out in a state of fright, not knowing where he was going, so God, exalted is He, sent an angel who guided him to the road. In some of the exegetical works: he went out barefoot, running for eight nights, with no provisions. Ibn 'Abbas said: "This was the first trial God imposed upon Musa: the sole of his foot fell off, and he began to eat herbs until he could see their greenness in his belly."

As for His saying: ﴿He said: "My Lord, deliver me from the wrongdoing people"﴾, its meaning is apparent.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 28, verse 22:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And when he turned toward Madyan﴾ means: toward (qabla) Madyan.

And His saying: ﴿He said, "It may be that my Lord will guide me to the right way"﴾ means: my Lord will direct me. ﴿The right way﴾ means: the middle of the road, and the middle of the road is the path that leads to the intended destination. Madyan is the name of a man to whom the town was attributed. The poet said concerning the cities: "The monks of Madyan, if they had seen you, would have come down, and the mountain goats from the peaks of the high cliffs..."

And the people of meanings (ahl al-ma'ani) said: "al-tawajjuh" is turning toward one of the directions.

And His saying: ﴿toward Madyan﴾: Abu 'Ubayda said: "nahwa Madyan" (in the direction of Madyan).

And His saying: ﴿It may be that my Lord will guide me to the right way﴾: Mujahid said: "the road of Madyan."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 28, verse 23:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And when he arrived at the water of Madyan﴾ means: when Musa arrived at the water of Madyan, and it is a well from which they would water their sheep and livestock.

His saying: ﴿he found upon it a community of people watering﴾ means: a group.

His saying: ﴿and he found beside them two women﴾ means: apart from the group, two women. It was also said: at a distance from the group, two women.

His saying: ﴿holding back﴾ means: they were restraining and keeping their sheep from mixing with the sheep of the people.

Qatadah said: "taduddan" means they were keeping the people away from their sheep. The poet said:

(They have stripped your staff, the Banu Tamim, so I do not know with which staff you could drive away)

Qatrib recited a line of poetry:

(I spend the night at the gate of rhymes, as if I were driving away with them a herd of wild animals, scattered)

His saying: ﴿What is your business?﴾ means: Musa said to the two women: "What is your business?" That is, "What is your matter?" The khatb (matter) is the important affair. He asked about them only because they were not watering the sheep together with the people.

His saying: ﴿They said: We do not water﴾ means: we do not water our sheep, and His saying: ﴿until the shepherds depart﴾ (and it was read: "until the shepherds depart", so His saying "until the shepherds depart" means: until the shepherds return with their sheep, and His saying "until the shepherds depart" [means] the shepherds drive their sheep away). Qatadah said: they would water their sheep with what remained of the people's water. Some of them said: they did not water their sheep because they disliked crowding with the men.

His saying: ﴿and our father is a very old man﴾, who cannot water the sheep. It is as if they made that their excuse. It was also said: they only said that to stir the heart of Musa so that he would water them. Ibn 'Abbas said: Musa arrived, that is, at the water of Madyan, and the greenness of the herbs could be seen in his bowels from emaciation.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 28, verse 24:

And His words: ﴿So he watered [their flocks] for them﴾. In the narrative it is said that the people had gone back with their flocks, and had covered the mouth of the well with a stone that only ten men could lift. Then Musa came, lifted the stone alone, and watered the flocks of the two women. It is also said that he drew one bucket and invoked blessing upon it, so that all the flock drank from it. Ibn Ishaq mentioned that Musa pushed through the people, held them back, and kept them away from the mouth of the well, and watered the flocks of the two women.

And His words: ﴿Then he turned back to the shade﴾. It is said that it was the shade of a tree. It is also said that it was the shade of a wall without a roof.

And His words: ﴿and said, "My Lord, indeed I am, for whatever good You would send down to me, in need"﴾. The exegetes unanimously agree that he asked God for food because of his hunger. Ibn Abbas said: a morsel of bread, or a handful of dates. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: there was no one on the face of the earth more noble than him, and he was in need of half a date. Mujahid said: he asked for bread. In some reports it is related that God brought forth for the bread the blessings of the heavens and the earth. It is also reported from some of them: "Were it not for bread, God would not be worshipped." The Arabs call bread "Jabir" (the one who mends hunger), and one of them said in verse:

(Do not blame me, but blame Jabir... for Jabir has burdened me with the noon heat.)

He means: working in the midday heat.

The Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Qur'an) on Surah 28, verse 25:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Then one of the two women came to him﴾. In the verse there is an omission, namely that the two women returned to their father. Most of the people of tafsir (exegesis) hold that their father was Shu'ayb, the Prophet, upon him be peace. Al-Hasan al-Basri said: he was a man from among those who believed in Shu'ayb. Some of them said: he was the son of Shu'ayb's brother. When the two returned to their father quickly, he disapproved of their early return, so they told him the story of the man, and he sent one of them to summon him.

And His saying: ﴿walking bashfully﴾. 'Amr ibn Maymun narrated from Umar that he said: she was not a brazen woman of the kind who go out and come in freely, but she placed her sleeve over her face out of modesty.

And His saying: ﴿She said: Indeed my father invites you, that he may reward you the recompense of what you gave us to drink﴾. That is, that he may feed you and reward you with the recompense of what you gave us to drink, i.e., in return for what you gave us to drink. Abu Hazim Salamah ibn Dinar said: When Musa heard this, he wished not to go, but he was hungry, and found no alternative to going. The woman walked and Musa walked behind her. The wind kept blowing her garment and outlining her hips, and Musa disliked that. He said: "O servant of Allah, walk behind me and direct me on the way." She did so. When Musa reached the house of Shu'ayb, the meal was ready, and he said: "O young man, sit down and eat." He said: "God forbid! We are a household that does not seek any worldly compensation for deeds of the Hereafter." Shu'ayb said to him: "This is my custom and the custom of my forefathers: we host guests and feed people." So he sat and ate. All of this is the saying of Abu Hazim.

And His saying: ﴿So when he came to him and related to him the narrative﴾. That is: what he had encountered from Pharaoh and his command, from beginning to end.

And His saying: ﴿Fear not; you have escaped from the wrongdoing people﴾. He said this only because Pharaoh had no authority over Madyan. "The wrongdoing people" refers to Pharaoh and his folk.

He said: "She said, 'O my father, hire him; indeed the best one you can hire is the strong and trustworthy one.'" — no, let me translate the passage as it stands.

**Translation:**

Allah's saying: ﴿One of the two women said, "O my father, hire him. Indeed, the best one to hire is the strong, the trustworthy."﴾ That is, hire him to tend the sheep.

In the narrative (al-qissa): Shu'ayb said to his daughter, "What makes you know of his strength and his trustworthiness?" She said, "As for his strength, it is that he lifted a stone which only ten men could lift. As for his trustworthiness, it is that he said to me, 'Walk behind me, lest the wind shape your body.'" It is also said: "The strong is in what is entrusted to him, and the trustworthy is in what is deposited with him."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 28, verse 27:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, I wish to marry you to one of these two daughters of mine﴾. Most of the people of tafsir (exegesis) said: he married him to the younger of the two, whose name was Safura', and she is the one who went to call Musa.

And His words: ﴿on condition that you serve me﴾, meaning: that you be my hired worker (ajir). It was also said: on condition that you compensate me. ﴿For eight years﴾, meaning: eight years.

His words: ﴿But if you complete ten, it is from you﴾, meaning: it is a voluntary act of kindness from you.

And His words: ﴿And I do not intend to burden you﴾, meaning: I do not require you to complete the ten years except that you do so voluntarily.

And His words: ﴿You will find me, God willing, among the righteous﴾, meaning: those who will be kind to you (al-rafiqin bika). This is like His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Take my place among my people and set things right﴾, meaning: be gentle (irfuq).

"The saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿He said, 'That is between me and you.'﴾ That is: this condition is between me and you. ﴿Whichever of the two terms I fulfil﴾ That is: whichever of the two terms I complete, and "mā" is extraneous (ṣila).

As for His saying: ﴿then there shall be no transgression against me﴾ That is: I shall not seek more than that. And His saying: ﴿and Allah is Witness (wakīl) over what we say﴾ That is: a witness. It has also been said: a guardian (ḥafīẓ).

It has been narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "Mūsā hired himself out for the food of his belly and the chastity of his private parts." And in some reports: the Prophet (ﷺ) was asked, "Which of the two terms did Mūsā fulfil?" He said: "The more complete and the more perfect of them."

Shaddād ibn Aws narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ): "Shu'ayb wept until he went blind, so Allah restored his sight to him (then he wept until he went blind, so Allah restored his sight to him), then he wept until he went blind. Allah, the Exalted, said: 'Why do you weep, O Shu'ayb? Out of fear of the Fire, or out of desire for Paradise?' He said: 'No, O Lord, but I love You.' Some of them said: 'Out of longing for Your meeting.' He said: 'O Shu'ayb, for that reason I made Mūsā, My interlocutor, your servant.'" The report is gharīb (strange).

As for the story of the staff: Shu'ayb said to his daughter: "Give Mūsā a staff so that he may strengthen himself with it in tending the sheep." Shu'ayb had a staff that he had entrusted to an angel, and Shu'ayb's daughter entered, and this staff came into her hand, and she went out with it. Shu'ayb said: "Return this staff and take another staff." She returned it, and she wanted to take another staff, but this staff fell into her hand, three times in this manner. So Shu'ayb gave the staff to Mūsā, and Mūsā went out with the staff. Then the Shaykh regretted, went after him, and asked him to return the staff to him, but Mūsā refused. They said: "Let us have recourse to the first one who meets us." A king met them in the form of a man, (and he judged that) the staff be cast down, and whoever is able to lift it, it is his. Mūsā cast down the staff, and Shu'ayb came to take it but was unable to lift it, while Mūsā came and took it and departed with the staff. This was related by Wahb, Ibn Isḥāq and others.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 28, verse 29:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So when Musa had fulfilled the term and set out with his family﴾. Regarding the story: when Musa had completed the term and Shu'ayb gave his daughter to him, Musa said to the woman, "Ask your father to let some of the sheep be ours." She asked her father for this, and Shu'ayb said, "Every offspring born this year that is not of their (the sheep's) colour (shiyah) is yours." It was also said: "Whatever is born speckled (balqa') is yours both." So Musa came to the water from which the sheep drank, and placed the staff in the water. It is narrated that whenever a sheep came to drink, he would strike its flank with the staff, and so all of them gave birth that year to offspring not of their colour, and he said, "They have given birth to speckled ones." Then Musa, peace be upon him, asked Shu'ayb's permission to return to Egypt to visit his mother and brother, and he gave him leave. So he set out with his family towards the side of Egypt.

And His saying: ﴿He perceived a fire from the side of the Mount (al-Tur)﴾. It is narrated that Musa was a man of jealous nature (ghayyur), and he used to travel with the caravan by night and separate from them by day. When the night came in which God willed to honour him, he lost the way, for the darkness intensified and the cold grew severe, and he was cut off from the caravan. So he began striking the flint (zand) but it would not kindle. Then he perceived a fire from the direction of al-Tur; it was a light and was not in fact a fire. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿He perceived a fire from the side of the Mount﴾, that is, he saw (absara).

And His saying: ﴿He said to his family, "Wait, I have perceived a fire"﴾, that is, I have seen a fire.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿That perhaps I may bring you from it some news﴾, that is, news about the way, since he had lost the way. And His saying: ﴿Or a brand from the fire﴾, that is, a piece of fire. It was also said: a stick with fire at its head.

And His saying: ﴿That you may warm yourselves﴾, that is, that you may warm yourselves by it, so that the cold may leave you. It is said: "It is better than the warmth (al-sala) in winter."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 28, verse 30:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿When he came to it, he was called from the right side of the valley﴾, i.e., the right side of Musa (Moses), and "shati'" (the bank, side) is the side.

And His saying: ﴿in the blessed spot﴾. It was called the blessed spot because Allah, Exalted is He, spoke to Musa there. If it is said: Why did He not describe the tree as blessed, when He said: ﴿from the tree﴾? We say: Because when blessing is mentioned in the spot, it has been mentioned in the tree too, so He mentioned the spot because it is more general.

And His saying: ﴿from the tree﴾. They said: the acacia tree (shajarat al-'awsaj) was the first tree planted on the earth. It was also said: it was the shajar al-'ulayq (a thorny climbing plant).

And His saying: ﴿O Musa, indeed I am Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾, i.e., Lord of the jinn, the humans, the angels and all creation.

And His saying: ﴿from the tree﴾. Al-Zajjaj, al-Nahhas and others said: Allah spoke to Musa from the tree without modality (bila kayf). And from al-Dahhak: from the direction of the tree. And according to the Mu'tazila: Allah created speech in the tree, and Musa heard that speech. This, according to us, is false, because Allah, Exalted is He, is the One who spoke to Musa, as the text has reported. And if it is in the manner they claim, then Allah would be a Creator and not a Speaker, because it is said "He created, so He is a Creator," and it is not said "He created, so He is a Speaker."

In the narrative: when Musa saw the fire, he left his family and his children and headed toward the fire. His family remained in that place for thirty years, until a shepherd passed by them and saw her (the daughter) sad and weeping, so he returned her to her father. Related by al-Naqqash in his tafsir.

And His saying: ﴿Indeed I am Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾ — we have explained it before.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 28, verse 31:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And throw down your staff﴾. In the narration: the staff was of the myrtle (ās) of Paradise. It came down to Adam, then from Adam to Nuh (Noah), then from Nuh to Ibrahim (Abraham), then from Ibrahim to Shu'ayb. No one would take it except that a prophet, and if anyone other than a prophet took it, it would devour him. On it was written in Syriac: "I am the First, I am the Last, I am the Living who never dies."

And His saying: ﴿So when he saw it moving﴾, meaning: quivering, ﴿as if it were a jann﴾. The jann is the small snake, and the thu'ban (th'ban) is the great snake.

We have already mentioned the reconciliation between the two verses. Some have said: at the beginning of the matter it was a small snake, then it kept growing until it became a thu'ban.

And His saying: ﴿he turned back in flight﴾, meaning: out of fear. If it is asked: why did Musa fear while he was in such a position? We say: because he saw something contrary to the usual course, and whoever sees something contrary to the usual course and is afraid is excused. It has been related that when it became a snake, it swallowed what was around it of rocks and trees, and Musa heard the loud grinding of its teeth, so he fled.

And His saying: ﴿and he did not look back﴾, meaning: he did not turn around. And His saying: ﴿O Musa, come forward and do not fear; indeed you are among the secure﴾, its meaning is clear.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 28, verse 32:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Insert your hand into your bosom﴾, meaning: put your hand into your bosom. In the narrative, he was wearing an Egyptian woolen garment (mudra'a).

And His saying: ﴿it will come out white, without harm﴾. It is said: it came out with a radiance like the light of the sun.

And His saying: ﴿and draw your arm close to your side against fear﴾. ʿAtaʾ reported from Ibn ʿAbbas that its meaning is: place your hand upon your chest. The janah (wing, here meaning arm) is the hand. He said: "There is no one fearful after Musa except that when he places his hand upon his chest, his fear departs." Al-Farra' mentioned in his book that the janah here is the staff, and its meaning is: draw your staff close to you. It is well known that the janah is the upper arm (ʿadd). It is also said: the whole hand. It is also said: what is beneath the armpit. When a fearful person draws his hand close to himself, his fear lightens. From Abu ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAla' it is reported that ar-rahb is the sleeve (kumm), so the meaning of the verse according to this is: draw your staff and your hand that is in your sleeve close to you, for We have made them two signs for you. It is read "min al-rahb." It is also said that ar-rahb and ar-rahb (with the vowel variants) have one meaning, like ar-rushd and ar-rushd. The apparent meaning of it is that it is fear.

And His saying: ﴿These two are proofs from your Lord﴾, meaning: these two are signs and arguments from your Lord.

And His saying: ﴿to Pharaoh and his chiefs﴾, meaning: and his followers.

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, they have been a defiantly disobedient people﴾, meaning: they went out of obedience.
And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿He said, "My Lord, I killed a man among them, so I fear that they will kill me."﴾ He means: the Copt.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 28, verse 34:

And His saying: ﴿And my brother Aaron, he is more eloquent in tongue than I﴾. The people of tafsir (exegesis) said: There was a knot (ʿuqdah) in Moses' tongue from the time when he seized the beard of Pharaoh, and then he took the ember and placed it in his mouth, as we mentioned before.

And His saying: ﴿So send him with me as a helper (ridʾ)﴾, meaning: a supporter. ﴿To confirm me﴾, meaning: confirming me. It was also read as "yuṣaddiqunī" with a sukun on the qaf, meaning: if they deny me, he will confirm me.

And His saying: ﴿Indeed I fear that they will deny me﴾, meaning: Pharaoh and his people.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 28, verse 35:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿He said, "We will strengthen your arm through your brother"﴾. This is by way of illustration, since the strength of the hand lies in the upper arm (al-'adud). In the speech transmitted from the Arabs, a man was told, "Your father has died," and he said, "I have taken possession of myself." It was said to him, "Your son has died," and he said, "My heart has been emptied." It was said, "Your wife has died," and he said, "My bed has been renewed." It was said, "Your brother has died," and he said, "My back has been broken." The poet said:

(Your brother, your brother, for whoever has no brother
is like one who runs to battle without a weapon.)

(And the son of a man's paternal uncle, know that he is his wing,
and can the falcon rise without a wing?)

God placed the brother before all other relatives in His saying: ﴿On the Day a man will flee from his brother﴾, because a person inclines most to his brother, is most at ease with him, and finds most comfort in him.

As for His saying: ﴿and We will give you both authority (sultan)﴾, it means proof (hujjah).

As for His saying: ﴿so they will not reach you both by Our signs﴾, it means they will not reach you both because of Our signs. It is also said that there is inversion (taqdim wa ta'khir) in the verse, and its intended sense is: "We will give you both authority by Our signs, so they will not reach you both."

As for His saying: ﴿You two and whoever follows you will be the victors﴾, the victors are over Pharaoh and his people.

And His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So when Moses came to them with Our signs, clear ones﴾, i.e., evident.

And His saying: ﴿They said, "This is nothing but fabricated magic"﴾, i.e., invented.

And His saying: ﴿"We never heard of this among our forefathers, the earlier ones"﴾, i.e., those who had passed away.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 28, verse 37:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And Moses said, "My Lord knows best who has come with guidance from Him"﴾ mean: "My Lord knows best who has come with the guidance; and I am the one who came with guidance from Him."

His words: ﴿and he for whom the final outcome of the abode will be﴾ mean: "And He knows best the one for whom the final outcome of the abode will be," and that is Paradise.

His words: ﴿Indeed, the wrongdoers will not succeed﴾ mean: whoever associates partners with Allah will not be made happy.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 28, verse 38:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And Pharaoh said, "O chiefs, I know of no god for you other than myself."﴾ It is said: between the making of this statement and his saying, ﴿I am your most exalted lord﴾, there was a span of forty years.

And His saying: ﴿So kindle for me, O Haman, [a fire] upon the clay﴾, meaning: bake the clay for me until it becomes bricks (ājurr). It is said that he was the first to make bricks (al-ājur).

And His saying: ﴿And make for me a tower (ṣarḥ)﴾, meaning: a lofty palace; and it is said: a minaret (manāra).

And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿That I may ascend to the god of Moses﴾, meaning: that I may reach him and attain him.

In the narrative: the height of the tower was something great. It is mentioned in some exegetical works that the tower of Pharaoh had a height of five thousand and fifty cubits (dhirā'), and a width of three thousand-odd cubits.

Pharaoh was unable to stand at its top, for fear that the wind would blow it down. al-Suddi mentioned that Pharaoh ascended that tower and shot an arrow toward the sky, and it returned to him smeared with blood, and he said: "I have killed the god of Moses."

And His saying: ﴿And indeed, I think he is among the liars﴾, meaning: I think he is among the liars in his claim that there is a god of the earth and of creation other than me.

Almost all of this passage is Qur'anic text or a short gloss, so I'll translate it as it stands.

God's words, "And he and his soldiers were arrogant in the land without right, and they thought that they would not be returned to Us" (Qur'an 28:39). That is, they would not be brought back (لَا يَنْقَلِبُون).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 28, verse 40:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So We seized him and his soldiers and threw them into the sea.﴾ That is: We cast them into the sea.

And His saying: ﴿So look at how was the end of the wrongdoers.﴾ He means: Pharaoh and his people.

Almost-literal translation of the passage:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And We made them leaders calling to the Fire﴾, meaning: leaders (qādah).

And His saying: ﴿And on the Day of Resurrection they will not be helped﴾, meaning: they will not be able to prevent (yamna'ūna) the punishment from them.

And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We made a curse follow them in this world﴾, meaning: We made the punishment in this world follow them as a curse.

And His saying: ﴿And on the Day of Resurrection they will be among the despised﴾, meaning: those who are punished. It is also said: "among the disfigured," meaning: by blackness of face and blueness of eye.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 28, verse 43:

His words, may He be exalted: ﴿And We certainly gave Moses the Book﴾, meaning: the Torah. And His words: ﴿after We had destroyed the earlier generations﴾, who were the people of Noah, ʿAd, Thamud, the people of Lot, the people of Shuʿayb, and others.

His words: ﴿as insights for mankind﴾, meaning: proofs for people.

His words: ﴿and a guidance and a mercy, so that they might remember﴾, meaning: that they might take heed through these proofs.

His words, may He be exalted: ﴿And you were not on the western side﴾, meaning: you were not in the region of the mountain that lies toward the west. His words: ﴿when We conveyed to Moses the command﴾, meaning: We settled the matter with Moses, and that was by sending him to Pharaoh and his people.

Translation of the passage:

And His saying: ﴿And you were not among the witnesses﴾, meaning: present at that place. The meaning of this is that you were neither a witness nor present at that place, and this knowledge [came] to you from Us.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 28, verse 45:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿But We produced generations, and the life span grew long for them﴾. It is narrated from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri that he said: "Allah, exalted is He, did not destroy any nation after His sending down the Torah to Musa except the town that transgressed on the Sabbath, so they were transformed," meaning: the people of that town.

And His saying: ﴿nor were you a dweller among the people of Madyan﴾, i.e., residing among them.

And His saying: ﴿reciting to them Our verses﴾. He said this because Shu'ayb used to recite to them the verses of Allah. It was said: this refers to Musa, but the first (view) is more apparent. And His saying: ﴿but We were senders [of messengers]﴾, i.e., We are the ones who sent them.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 28, verse 46:

The Almighty's saying: ﴿And you were not on the side of the Mount when We called out﴾. It is narrated from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said regarding the meaning of this verse: Indeed Allah, exalted is He, said: "O community of Muhammad, I gave you before you asked Me, I answered you before you called upon Me, and I forgave you before you sought forgiveness from Me." This is the meaning of the calling out. Some of them transmitted this with a chain traced back to the Prophet (ﷺ).

Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: The meaning of His saying, ﴿We called out﴾, is that He said to this community, while they were in the loins of their fathers: "Believe in Muhammad when I send him."

And in the narrative: when Musa heard this from Allah, exalted is He, he said: "My Lord, I came only as a delegate for the community of Muhammad."

As for His saying, ﴿But it was a mercy from your Lord﴾, it has been established from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "Indeed Allah, exalted is He, wrote a book two thousand years before He created Adam, and it is with Him above His Throne: 'My mercy has preceded My wrath.'"

As for the Almighty's saying, ﴿that you may warn a people to whom no warner had come before you, that they might remember﴾, its meaning is apparent.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 28, verse 47:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿And if not that a calamity should afflict them for what their hands have sent forth, and they should say, "Our Lord, why did You not send to us a messenger so we could follow Your signs and be among the believers?"﴾ The meaning of the verse is: were it not for their saying this, and their argument based on the absence of the sending of messengers, We would have hastened the punishment upon them. Some scholars said: there is inversion (taqdim wa ta'khir) in the verse, and the intended construction is: "And if not that they would say, 'Our Lord, why did You not send to us a messenger so we could follow Your signs and be among the believers,' a calamity would have afflicted them for what their hands have sent forth." The calamity (musibah) here means the punishment ('uqubah).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 28, verse 48:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Then when the truth came to them from Us﴾. Concerning "the truth" there are two opinions: one of them is that it is Muhammad, and the other is that it is the Qur'an.

His saying: ﴿They said﴾, meaning: the polytheists said, ﴿"Why was he not given"﴾, i.e., "Why was he not given" ﴿"the like of what was given to Musa"﴾, i.e., of the staff and the white hand.

His saying: ﴿"Did they not disbelieve in what was given to Musa before?"﴾ meaning: the polytheists disbelieved in Musa.

His saying: ﴿"They said: two sorceries that support each other"﴾, meaning: Musa and Muhammad. Mujahid said: Musa and Harun. It has been recited as "two sorceries that support each other" (siHRān tazāharā). Opinion differs regarding "two sorceries" (li-siHRayn): one opinion is that they are the Torah and the Qur'an, and the other is that they are the Torah and the Gospel.

His saying: ﴿"Support each other"﴾, i.e., assist one another. This applies to "two sorcerers" literally, and to "two sorceries" by way of extension (al-tawassu'). His saying: ﴿"Indeed, we are disbelievers in all of it"﴾, i.e., deniers.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 28, verse 49:

And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Say: "Then bring a Book from Allah that is better guided than these two, and I will follow it, if you are truthful."﴾ He means: from the Torah and the Qur'an.

And His saying: ﴿I will follow it﴾ means: follow the Book that you have brought from Allah.

And His saying: ﴿if you are truthful﴾ its meaning is: that the truth is with you.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 28, verse 50:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And if they do not respond to you﴾, meaning: they have not brought what you asked for. And His saying: ﴿then know that they only follow their own desires﴾. The people of knowledge (ahl al-ma'rifa) agree that desire (hawa) is a destructive path.

It has been narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "The thing I fear most for you is miserliness that is obeyed, desire that is followed, and every person being pleased with his own opinion."

His saying: ﴿And who is more astray than one who follows his desire without guidance from Allah?﴾, meaning: without clear proof from Allah. The verse indicates that it is possible for desire to coincide with the truth, though this is rare. It has been related that a certain shaykh was asked about a desire that coincided with a truth, and he said: "It is the zabd with narsiyan, and narsiyan is a type of date in Basra, the best of its kind."

His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people﴾, meaning: the polytheists. The verse is evidence that the Prophet (ﷺ) demanded of them that they bring a book like his book, and he challenged them with this repeatedly, and they did not bring it. Had they been able, they would have brought it, even by sacrificing their souls and their wealth. Had they brought it, that would have been recognized, and it would have spread among the caravans.

And We have certainly made the word follow up for them (Qur'an 28:51). That is: We mentioned to them the destruction of the past nations, so that some of them were connected to others in disbelief, and the punishment of some of them was connected to the punishment of others.

As for His saying, exalted is He: ﴿so that they might take heed﴾, that is: [they might be admonished].

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 28, verse 52:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿Those to whom We gave the Book before it, they believe in it﴾. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: They are a people from among the believers of Abyssinia (al-Habasha), who believed in the Prophet, came to Madina, and fought alongside him.

And it is narrated from [Ibn] 'Abbas, who said: The verse was revealed concerning eighty people from the People of the Book, forty from Najran, thirty-two from Abyssinia, and eight from Syria.

Some of them said: The verse was revealed concerning a people who used to seek the religion before the Prophet came. When he was sent, they believed in him and said. Among them were 'Abd Allah ibn Salam, Salman, al-Jarud al-'Abdari, and others.

And His words: ﴿they believe in it﴾, that is, in the Book. It has also been said: in Muhammad.

Almost-verbatim translation follows.

The Exalted's saying: ﴿And when it is recited to them﴾ — meaning: the Qur'an — {they say: "We believe in it. Indeed it is the truth from our Lord. Indeed, we were Muslims (submitters) before it"}. Meaning: monotheists (muwahhidun).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 28, verse 54:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Those will be given their reward twice, because they were patient﴾ means: the reward of belief in the first Book, and the reward of belief in the second Book.

It is established by the narration of Abu Musa al-Ash'ari from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "Three will be given their reward twice: a man who believed in the first Book and then in the second; a slave who fulfilled the right of Allah and the right of his masters; and a man who had a slave-girl, disciplined her and did so well in her discipline, taught her and did so well in her teaching, then freed her and married her."

In the exegesis it is related that the People of the Book who believed boasted to the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) with this verse, saying: "Allah, exalted is He, gives us our reward twice and gives you the reward once." So Allah, exalted is He, revealed: ﴿O you who believe, fear Allah and believe in His Messenger; He will give you a double portion of His mercy﴾, the verse.

His saying: ﴿because they were patient﴾ means: they were patient upon the truth and did not deviate from it. His saying: ﴿and they repel evil with good﴾ means: with the saying "there is no god but Allah" they repel polytheism; it is also said: with what is right they repel what is wrong, with goodness they repel evil, and it is said: with forbearance they repel the ignorance of the ignorant.

His saying: ﴿and from what We have provided them, they spend﴾ means: they spend in obedience to Allah.

It is narrated that the people from Abyssinia who believed, when they came to Medina and struggled, asked the Prophet (ﷺ) for permission to return to Abyssinia and to carry their wealth, and he permitted them. So they went, carried the wealth, and spent.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 28, verse 55:

And His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿And when they hear vain talk, they turn away from it﴾. That is, the false speech. It is also said: the polytheists used to revile the believers among the People of the Book and would say: "Woe to you! You have abandoned your religion and followed a youth from among us." This is the meaning of the vain talk mentioned in the verse.

And His saying: ﴿And they say: "To us our deeds, and to you your deeds"﴾. That is, to us our religion, and to you your religion. It is also said: to you your foolishness, and to us our forbearance.

And His saying: ﴿Peace be upon you﴾. The intended meaning of "peace" here is not the greeting (taḥiyyah); rather, this peace is the peace of disengagement (salām al-mutārakah). It is said its meaning is: "You are safe from our opposing you with ignorance and folly."

It is related from some of the early predecessors (salaf) that when he was reviled, he would say: "Peace, peace." And it is related from some of them: that is, they spoke words from which they would be safe.

And His saying: ﴿We do not seek the ignorant﴾. That is, we do not enter into the ignorance of the ignorant.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 28, verse 56:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, you do not guide whom you like﴾. Most of the people of tafsir (exegesis) say that the verse was revealed concerning Abu Talib. It is authentically related, through the narration of Abu Hurairah from the Prophet, that when death came to Abu Talib, the Prophet entered upon him while Abu Jahl, Abdullah ibn Abi Umayyah and others were with him. The Messenger of Allah said: "O uncle, say: There is no god but Allah, a word by which I may argue on your behalf before Allah." Abu Jahl and Abdullah ibn [Abi] Umayyah said to him: "Do you turn away from the religion of the forefathers (al-ashyakh)?" The Messenger of Allah kept repeating that to him, and they kept saying it too, until the last thing he said was: "I am upon the religion of the forefathers." By "the forefathers" (al-ashyakh) is meant Abd al-Muttalib, Hashim and Abd Manaf. This report is in the two Sahihs. Muslim, in his Sahih, related that the Prophet entered upon Abu Talib when death had come to him, and said: "O uncle, I bear witness that there is no god but Allah; I will intercede for you on the Day of Resurrection." He said: "Were it not that the women of Quraysh would reproach me, saying, 'He panicked at death,' I would have brought you comfort by it (le-aqarrat bihā ʿaynayk)." In another narration: "Were it not that the women of Quraysh would reproach you, and that it would be a blemish upon you, I would have brought you comfort by it." The first is in the Sahih. Then Allah, Exalted is He, revealed: ﴿Indeed, you do not guide whom you like﴾, meaning: whom you like to be guided. It was also said: whom you love because of his kinship. ﴿But Allah guides whom He wills﴾, meaning: He guides to His religion whom He wills.

And from [Sa'id ibn Abi Rashid]: that Heraclius sent a messenger from Tanukh to the Messenger of Allah. He came to him while he was at Tabuk, carrying Heraclius' letter. The Prophet said to him: "O brother of Tanukh, embrace Islam." He said: "I am the messenger of a king; I came from his presence, and I dislike to return to him contrary to what I came with." The Prophet laughed and recited His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, you do not guide whom you like, but Allah guides whom He wills﴾.

His saying: ﴿And He is most knowing of those who are guided﴾, meaning: He is most knowing of those for whom guidance has been decreed.

"And they say: 'If we follow the guidance with you, we will be snatched away from our land.'" Al-ikhtitaf (snatching) is the taking away of something swiftly. It is said that the one who made this statement was al-Harith ibn Nawfal ibn Abd Manaf. He said to the Prophet (ﷺ): "We know that what you have brought is true, but if we embrace Islam with you, we will not be able to withstand the Arabs; for we are a morsel for them (ukalat ra's), and the Arabs will come at us from every side, and we will not be able to withstand them."

His saying: "Did We not establish for them a secure sanctuary (haraman amina)?" means: a place of security. It is well known that gazelles are safe there from wolves, and doves from kites.

His saying: "To which are brought the fruits of all things" means: the fruits of everything are gathered to it. It is said: "I collected (jabaytu) the water in the basin," meaning I gathered it.

His saying: "As a provision from Us" means: We provided them with it as a provision from Us.

His saying: "But most of them do not know" means: what I say is true. The meaning of the verse is: despite your disbelief, We made you secure in the sanctuary, so how would We frighten you when you embrace Islam?

Mujahid said: At the Maqam (Station of Ibrahim) a book was found in which was written: "I am Allah, Possessor of Bakkah. I shaped it on the day I created the sun and the moon, and I made it sacred on the day I created the heavens and the earth. I surrounded it with seven angels, who are upright (hunafa'). Its provision comes to it from three paths. It is blessed for it in meat and water. The first to make it lawful are its people."

We have explained earlier that the man from the people of the sanctuary would go out and no one would confront him, and it is said: "These are the people of Allah."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 28, verse 58:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And how many a town have We destroyed, [the people of] which had been insolent in their livelihood﴾, meaning: how many people of a town, who had been insolent in their livelihood, meaning: they had been insolent in their livelihood. And al-Farra' said: their livelihood made them insolent (abtarathā ma'īshatuhā).

And His saying: ﴿So those are their dwellings, not inhabited after them except a little﴾, meaning: We ruined most of them. And it is said: the meaning of "little" here is that the traveller stops at a ruined dwelling and remains in it for a day or part of a day.

And His saying: ﴿And We are the inheritors﴾ — we have already explained it.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 28, verse 59:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And your Lord would never destroy the cities until He sent in their mother (town) a messenger﴾. That is, Makkah. It is also said: "in their mother a messenger" means: in its greatest (city) of all the rest of the world, a messenger.

And His saying: ﴿reciting to them Our verses﴾ — its meaning is well known.

And His saying: ﴿And We would never destroy the cities unless their people were wrongdoers﴾. That is: We did not destroy the people of any town except after they had committed sin.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 28, verse 60:

His statement, exalted is He: ﴿And whatever you have been given is but the enjoyment (matā') of the worldly life and its adornment﴾. The word matā' (enjoyment, provision) has two meanings. One of the two meanings is al-mut'ah (enjoyment, pleasure), and the other meaning is that which one furnishes or equips oneself with (mā yatta'athth bihi).

His statement: ﴿and its adornment﴾, that is: and the adornment of the worldly life.

His statement: ﴿But what is with God is better and more lasting. Will you not then use your reason?﴾, that is: will you not then look, so that you might understand that what endures is better than what perishes.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 28, verse 61:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿Is one to whom We have promised a good promise, and he is to meet it, [equal to one We have given the enjoyment of worldly life]?﴾ Al-Suddi said: This was revealed concerning Hamza and Abu Jahl. Others said: It was revealed concerning the Prophet (ﷺ) and Abu Jahl.

His words ﴿then he is to meet it﴾ mean: he will be meeting it and arriving at it. The good promise is Paradise.

His words ﴿like one whom We have given the enjoyment of worldly life﴾ mean: We have given him the enjoyment of worldly life, and then his return will be to the Fire. This is the meaning of His words ﴿then on the Day of Resurrection he will be among those brought forth﴾, meaning: among those brought forth to the Fire.

And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And on the Day He calls to them and says, "Where are My partners whom you used to claim?"﴾ It means: Where are My partners whom you used to claim that they are My partners?

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 28, verse 63:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Those against whom the Word has been justified will say﴾ means: the word of punishment has become binding upon them.

And His saying: ﴿Our Lord, these are the ones whom we led astray﴾ means: we invited them to error (al-ghayy).

And His saying: ﴿We led them astray just as we ourselves were led astray﴾ means: we misguided them just as we were misguided.

And His saying: ﴿We disassociate ourselves before You; it was not us that they worshipped﴾ means: they did not worship us, but we invited them and they responded.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 28, verse 64:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And it will be said: "Call upon your partners"﴾ means: it will be said to the disbelievers: "Call upon your partners," i.e., the idols. And the meaning of His saying ﴿your partners﴾ is: "My partners" according to your claim.

And His saying: ﴿So they will call upon them, but they will not respond to them﴾ means: they will not respond to them.

And His saying: ﴿And they will see the punishment; if only they had been guided﴾ means: if only they had been guided, they would not have seen the punishment.
And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And on the day He will call them and say, "What was your response to the messengers?"﴾ That is: the disbelievers are called.

[Al-Sam'ani's commentary on Surah 28, verse 66]

And His saying: ﴿Then the reports will be obscured for them that day﴾, i.e., the proofs (al-hujaj). It is as if, when they find no proof, they are rendered incapable of them.

And His saying: ﴿So they will not question one another﴾ — we have already explained that this is in some of the situations (mawatin). It is also said: they will not question one another with the questioning of kinship and compassion. And it is said: no one will ask another (to bear) his sin, i.e., one does not bear another's burden, because he will not find (anything to bear it with).

And His saying: ﴿As for one who repents, believes, and does righteousness, it may be that he will be among the successful﴾. That is: among the fortunate and the successful. In some works of tafsir (Qur'anic exegesis), it is stated that عَسَى (ʿasā, "perhaps") is obligatory (wājib) throughout the Qur'an, except in His saying: ﴿It may be that his Lord, if he divorces you, will give him in exchange wives better than you﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 28, verse 68:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And your Lord creates whatever He wills and chooses.﴾ That is: He creates whatever He wills of creation, and chooses whom He wills for prophethood. It is said that this verse was revealed concerning al-Walid ibn al-Mughira, when he said: ﴿Why was this Qur'an not sent down upon a great man from the two towns?﴾ By this he meant al-Walid ibn al-Mughira himself and Urwa ibn Mas'ud al-Thaqafi. The two towns are Makkah and al-Ta'if. So God, exalted is He, revealed this verse.

His saying: ﴿They have no choice.﴾ That is: the choosing belongs to Him, and they have no choice over God. It was also said that this verse was revealed concerning their sacrifices to the idols, for they would set aside the fattest for the idols and set aside what was worse for God.

His saying: ﴿Glory be to God, and exalted is He above what they associate with Him.﴾ He declared Himself free of what the polytheists attribute to Him.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 28, verse 69:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And your Lord knows what their breasts conceal﴾, meaning: what their breasts hide; ﴿and what they reveal﴾, meaning: what they make apparent.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 28, verse 70:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And He is Allah; there is no deity except Him. To Him belongs praise in the first and the last⁠—﴾ meaning: in this world and the Hereafter. It is also said: "in the first and the last" means: on earth and in the heavens.

As for His words: ﴿And to Him belongs the judgment﴾ meaning: the decisive judgment among the servants.

As for His words: ﴿And to Him you will be returned﴾ we have already explained it.

"The saying of Allah, Exalted is He: ﴿Say: Have you considered, if Allah made the night perpetual for you until the Day of Resurrection﴾, meaning: continuously.

And His saying: ﴿Who is a deity other than Allah that could bring you light?﴾, meaning: daylight.

And His saying: ﴿Then will you not hear?﴾, meaning: will you not understand. It is also said: "Will you not hear?" means listening with comprehension."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 28, verse 72:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Say: Have you considered, if Allah made the day perpetual over you until the Day of Resurrection, what god other than Allah could bring you a night in which you rest? Will you not then see?﴾ Its meaning is: "perpetual," i.e., continuous. And His saying: ﴿Who is a god other than Allah that could bring you night in which you rest? Will you not then see?﴾ Its meaning is: "Will you not then know?" If someone says: What is the benefit of the night in this world, when there is no night in Paradise? The answer to this is that the world is never free of the toil of obligations and duties, so it necessarily needs a time that leads to rest (from fatigue). As for Paradise, it is the place of enjoying pleasures, and there is no toil in it at all, so it has no need of a time that leads to rest at all.

Almighty God's words: ﴿And of His mercy He made for you the night and the day, that you might rest therein﴾, meaning: that you might rest during the night. And His words: ﴿and that you might seek of His bounty﴾, meaning: by day.

And His words: ﴿so that perhaps you will be thankful﴾, meaning: that you may be thankful for the blessings of God.

The saying of God, the Exalted: ﴿And on the day He calls to them and says, "Where are My partners whom you used to claim?"﴾ The meaning has already been explained. It is also possible that one call follows another in order to increase the rebuke and reproach.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 28, verse 75:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And We will draw out from every nation a witness﴾, meaning: We will extract from every nation a witness who will testify against them. The more apparent view is that the witness over every nation is their prophet.

And His saying: ﴿Then We will say, "Produce your proof."﴾ meaning: your argument and your evidence.

And His saying: ﴿So they will know that the truth belongs to Allah﴾ meaning: they will be unable to produce the argument, and they will know that the truth belongs to Allah.

And His saying: ﴿And what they used to invent will have deserted them﴾ meaning: what they used to invent in the world will have deserted them on the Day of Resurrection. The meaning of "dalla" (ḍalla, "to go astray, to be lost") here is: passed away and gone.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 28, verse 76:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, Qarun﴾. Qatadah and Ibn Jurayj said: He was the paternal cousin of Musa (Moses), a son of his uncle. Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: He was the son of Musa's brother, other than Harun (Aaron).

And His words: ﴿so he oppressed them﴾. Al-Dahhak said: That is, through polytheism (shirk). Shahr ibn Hawshab said: "He oppressed them" means he added a span to his garments over the garments of the people. Some of them said: He oppressed them through arrogance (takabbur). ﴿from among the people of Musa, so he oppressed them. And We gave him of the treasures such that its keys would weigh down a band of strong men, when﴾ and haughtiness. It is well known among the exegetes that Qarun was the most skilled reciter of the Torah among the Children of Israel and had a beautiful voice. Then he became a hypocrite. It is related that he said to Musa: "You have taken prophethood, and Harun has taken the altar and the office of the priesthood (al-hibarah); so what is my share?"

In the narrative: he gave a prostitute from among the Children of Israel two thousand dirhams and asked her to come to the assembly of the Children of Israel, with Musa among them, and to accuse him of having committed adultery with her. Some said: she should accuse him of having invited her to himself. She came and made that accusation against him. It is related that she became afraid and informed them that Qarun had given her money to make that claim. In the first narration: when she made that accusation against Musa, Musa became extremely angry and said to her: "By the One who sent down the Torah and split the sea, speak the truth." Then she became afraid and related the matter as it had happened. So Musa invoked Allah the Exalted against Qarun, and Allah the Exalted gave him power over him and made the earth subservient to him, as we shall mention.

And His words: ﴿And We gave him of the treasures such that its keys﴾. Concerning this there are two opinions: the first is that the keys (mafatih) are his treasuries, as in His words: ﴿and with Him are the keys of the unseen (mafatih al-ghayb)﴾, meaning the treasuries of the unseen. The second is that the keys (mafatih) are the bunches of keys to the treasuries (maqalid al-khaza'in). It is related from some of them that each key was the size of a finger, and that it would be carried by sixty mules; it is also said forty mules, and it is said forty men. And His words ﴿to weigh down﴾ mean: to burden the band. Abu 'Ubaydah said: this is an inversion (maqlub), and its sense is: "the band would be burdened by them." It is said: "Fulan was weighed down by such-and-such," meaning he rose up under its weight; and it is also said that its meaning is: "to weigh down the band."

As for the band (ʿusbah), there are several sayings: one is that they are seventy men; another, forty men; some said from ten to forty; some said six or seven; and some said ten, because the brothers of Yusuf said: "and we are a band (ʿusbah)," and they were ten. The ʿusbah in the language are the people whose members support one another.

And His words: ﴿with the band of men of strength (ula al-quwwah)﴾, meaning: those of might.

And His words: ﴿when his people said to him: "Do not exult"﴾, meaning: do not be boastful nor insolent; and "exult" (al-farah) here is joy without right.

And His words: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not love the exultant﴾, is clear.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Qur'an) on surah 28, verse 77:

His saying: ﴿But seek, through what Allah has given you, the Abode of the Hereafter﴾. Al-Hasan al-Basri said: "By seeking what is lawful (halal)." Al-Suddi said: "By charity and maintaining the ties of kinship." It is related from some of them that he said: "By drawing near to Allah through every means of drawing near."

His saying: ﴿And do not forget your share of this world﴾. That is: seek the Hereafter through what you do in this world. Its meaning is: work in this world for your Hereafter. Some of them said: "And do not forget your share of this world" means: by being content with what Allah has made lawful, rather than what Allah has forbidden. And in some of the supplications of the righteous: "O Allah, make me independent by Your lawful over Your unlawful, and by Your bounty over all others than You."

His saying: ﴿And do good as Allah has done good to you﴾. That is: and do good by obeying Allah, as Allah has done good to you with His blessings. It is also said: "And do good by seeking what is lawful, as Allah has done good to you with what is lawful."
