His saying: ﴿And do not seek corruption in the earth﴾. That is: by disobedience, for everyone who disobeys Allah has sought corruption in the earth.

His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not love the corrupters﴾. Its meaning is apparent.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 28, verse 78:

His words, may He be exalted: ﴿He said, "I have only been given it on account of knowledge I possess."﴾ On this there are several opinions. The first: God, exalted is He, gave me this wealth because of His favour in my knowledge. The second opinion: it is the knowledge of alchemy (al-kimiya').

In the tafsir of al-Naqqash: Musa (peace be upon him) taught Yusha' ibn Nun one third of alchemy, and taught Qarun one third of alchemy, and taught Harun one third of alchemy; so his wealth increased by this. The third opinion: "on account of knowledge I possess" means knowledge of the ways of gain and of management (of affairs).

And it is related from 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah that Qarun found a treasure of Yusuf, and his wealth was from this direction.

As for His words: ﴿Did he not know that God had already destroyed before him generations that were stronger than him in might and greater in accumulation?﴾ That is, (greater) in wealth.

And His words: ﴿And the guilty will not be asked about their sins﴾, that is, on the Day of Resurrection. If someone says: God, exalted is He, has said: ﴿So by your Lord, We will surely question them all﴾ and similar verses, whereas here He said: "And the guilty will not be asked about their sins." How then can the two verses be reconciled? The answer: we have explained that there are stations on the Day of Resurrection; in one station they are questioned, and in another station they are not questioned. It is said: they are not questioned with a question of seeking information; rather they are questioned with a question of rebuke and reproach. It is also said: they are not questioned as one who has an excuse in answering; rather they are questioned in the sense of displaying their ugly deeds so that they are disgraced before the heads of the gathering.

And from Qatadah, who said: The disbeliever is not brought to account; rather he is commanded to the Fire without reckoning or questioning. Some of them said: ﴿And the guilty will not be asked about their sins﴾ because they are recognised by their marks, as God, exalted is He, said: ﴿The guilty will be recognised by their marks﴾.

The words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿So he went out before his people in his adornment﴾. Adornment (al-zinah) is the splendour and radiance of this world.

It is related from Ibrahim al-Nakha'i that he said: Qarun and his people went out wearing red and yellow garments.

It is related from Muqatil that he said: He went out on a white mule, upon which was a gold saddle, and on the saddle was a covering of arjuwan (crimson cloth). With him were four thousand horsemen, mounted and dressed in arjuwanat, and with him were three hundred fair-skinned slave girls on white mules, adorned with jewellery.

It is related from some of them that he said: He went out with seventy thousand men, all wearing garments dyed with safflower (mu'as'faratan).

In some of the Musnads it is related from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "Four things were among the characteristics of Qarun's people: jaww (ornamented) sword-sheaths, wearing variegated slippers, arjuwan garments, and one of them would not look at the face of his servant out of arrogance."

It is related from 'Ata' that he said: Musa used to narrate to the Children of Israel and admonish them. Qarun went out with four thousand men on mules, in arjuwan garments, and passed by Musa. The Children of Israel turned towards him and were distracted from Musa. This grieved Musa, so he sent to him: "Why did you do this?" He replied: "I have been favoured with prophethood, and I have been favoured with wealth. If you wish, you may supplicate and I will supplicate." Then Musa invoked Allah, the Exalted, against Qarun, so Allah placed the earth under his command.

As for His words: ﴿Those who desired the life of this world said, "Oh, would that we had the like of what Qarun has been given! Indeed, he is one of great fortune."﴾ — i.e., a great share of this world.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 28, verse 80:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And those who had been given knowledge said, "Woe to you! The reward of Allah is better for those who believe and do righteous deeds. And none is granted it except the patient"﴾. That is: the reward of Allah in the Hereafter ﴿is better for those who believe and do righteous deeds. And none is granted it except the patient﴾. That is: righteous deeds are not bestowed except upon the patient. It is also said: "it" does not refer to righteous deeds but to this statement, the statement being His words: ﴿Woe to you! The reward of Allah is better for those who believe and do righteous deeds, and none is granted it except the patient﴾.

It is also said: the patient (al-sabirun) are those who restrained themselves from the adornment that the enemies of Allah were given, did not grieve over it, and did not wish for it.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 28, verse 81:

The words of God, Exalted is He: ﴿So We caused the earth to swallow him and his home﴾. In some tafsir works it is reported that Qarun said to Musa: "We have accepted for you the prophethood, but what about the (ceremonial) office of the priesthood (al-hibwa) for Harun? And if you have prophethood and Harun has the priesthood, then what about me?" Musa said: "I did not give him the priesthood; rather, God Exalted gave it to him." Qarun said: "I will not believe you in this until you show me a sign." So Musa commanded them, and they gathered their staffs, and he said: "Whoever's staff turns green, the priesthood belongs to him." Harun's staff turned green, and began to stir among the staffs. Qarun said: "This is from your sorcery, and this is not the first sorcery you have brought." At that point Musa invoked God against Qarun.

It is also narrated that when he (Qarun) hired the prostitute woman, until she claimed against Musa that he had committed adultery with her, or had invited her to indecency, Musa became angry and invoked God Exalted. In some accounts: there were with Qarun many people from the Banu Lawi. Musa came to them and said: "God has sent me to Qarun just as He sent me to Pharaoh, so whoever wants me, let him withdraw from him." All his people withdrew from him except two men from among his cousins who remained with him. Then Musa addressed the earth and said: "Take them!" The earth seized them up to their feet. Then he said: "Take them!" and it seized them up to their knees. Then he said: "Take them!" and it seized them up to their waists. Then he said: "Take them!" and it seized them up to their necks.

In the tafsir it is said: Qarun, throughout all of this, was calling on Musa for help and appealing to him by the ties of kinship, saying: "Have mercy on me!" Then (Musa) said: "Take them!" and the earth closed over them.

Qatadah said: "They keep sinking into the earth a cubit every day until the Day of Resurrection."

It is reported from Ibn 'Abbas that God said to Musa: "How hard is your heart! My servant called on you for help and you did not help him. Had he called on Me even once, I would have helped him."

In some reports: "I will not make the earth after you obedient to anyone."

Abu al-Husayn ibn Faris mentioned in his tafsir: when the earth seized Qarun up to his neck, Musa removed his sandals, struck his face with them, and said: "Go, O sons of Lawi!" and the earth closed over them.

He also mentioned that Yunus ibn Matta met him in the darkness of the earth when the fish was carrying him around, and Qarun said to him: "O Yunus, repent to God; you will find God at the first step you take back toward Him." Yunus said to him: "Why do you not repent?" He said: "I have made my repentance dependent upon my cousin."

As for His words, ﴿and his home﴾: it is reported that the Banu Isra'il said: "Musa only destroyed Qarun in order to seize his wealth, and the lands of his house were of silver, and the furnishings of its walls were of gold." So Musa commanded the earth until his house was brought forth, then commanded it until it was swallowed up with them, and the speech ended.

As for His words, ﴿and he had no company to help him﴾, i.e., no group, ﴿who could help him﴾, i.e., protect him, ﴿against God﴾.

As for His words, ﴿nor was he among those who could defend themselves﴾, i.e., among those who could resist, and its meaning: he was not able to defend himself, nor could anyone protect him from the punishment of God.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 28, verse 82:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And those who had wished to be in his place the day before began to say﴾ means: that they would be in his place and in his position.

And His saying: ﴿They say, "Woe! It is as if Allah..."﴾ and His saying: ﴿Wayka'anna﴾ (Wayka'anna). Regarding it there are several opinions. Al-Farra' said: "Wayka'anna" among the Arabs is an affirmation (taqrir), and its meaning is: "Do you not see that..." Al-Farra' related that a Bedouin woman said to her husband, "Where is your son?" He said to her, "Wayka'annahu (it is as if he is) behind the house," meaning: "Do you not see him behind the house?"

Some of them said that "wayka'annahu": the meaning of "wayk" is "woe to you" (waylaka), the lam has been dropped, and His saying ﴿annahu﴾ is a word of regret. As if the people, when they saw that state, regretted what they had wished for, then said: "Allah expands provision for whom He wills" meaning: "Indeed Allah expands provision for whom He wills and restricts (it)," i.e., He widens and narrows.

They recited, in support of what we have said of these meanings:

(Two women divorced ... when they saw me, they said: "What is with me? You have come to me with a denial")
(Woe! It is as if whoever has wealth is loved, and whoever is poor lives a life of harm)

They also recited the saying of 'Antarah concerning "wayk" meaning "woe to you":

(And indeed he has healed my soul and cured its sickness: the saying of the horsemen, "Woe to you, 'Antar, advance!")

It is well known in the exegeses, from the earlier scholars, that "Wayka'anna Allah" means: "Do you not see that Allah..." and Abu 'Ubaydah related the like of this.

His saying: ﴿Had Allah not been gracious to us, He would have caused the earth to swallow us up﴾ means: had Allah not bestowed His favour upon us, He would have caused the earth to swallow us as He caused it to swallow Qarun.

His saying: ﴿Wayka'annahu la yuflihu al-kafirun (Woe! It is as if the disbelievers do not prosper)﴾ has already been explained.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 28, verse 83:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿That is the Last Abode; We assign it to those who do not desire exaltation on earth﴾, meaning: arrogance. The root of arrogance (takabbur) is associating partners with Allah. Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Indeed, when it was said to them, "There is no deity except Allah," they were arrogant﴾. Among arrogance is lording it over people, belittling them, and treating them with contempt. It is also said that desiring exaltation is abandoning humility.

It was said: His saying, ﴿who do not desire exaltation on earth﴾, means: they do not grieve over its humiliation, nor do they compete for its might.

His saying, ﴿nor corruption﴾, means: acting in acts of disobedience. ʿIkrimah said: it is taking people's wealth without right.

His saying, ﴿and the final outcome is for the God-fearing﴾, means: Paradise is for the God-fearing. It was also said: the good final outcome is for the God-fearing. Zadhan narrated from ʿAli (may Allah be pleased with him) that he would walk and move about in the markets, helping the weak, supporting the oppressed, and passing by the grocer and the merchant, and the Qur'an would open up to him, and he would recite: ﴿That is the Last Abode; We assign it to those who do not desire exaltation on earth...﴾ to the end of the verse.

Also from him, he said: Whoever is pleased with the thong of his sandal over his brother's sandal-thong, he is among those who desire exaltation on earth.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 28, verse 84:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿Whoever comes with a good deed, he will have better than it﴾. The meaning is clear.

﴿And whoever comes with an evil deed, those who did evil deeds will not be recompensed except according to what they used to do﴾. That is: the sins (al-ma'asi). And it is related from Abdullah ibn Ubayd ibn Umayr that he said: How beautiful are good deeds after evil deeds, and how ugly are evil deeds after good deeds. The best of good deeds are good deeds following good deeds, and the worst of evil deeds are evil deeds following evil deeds.

It is well known from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he advised Mu'adh (may Allah be pleased with him), saying: "Fear Allah wherever you are, follow an evil deed with a good deed and it will erase it, and deal with people with good character."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 28, verse 85:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, He who has imposed upon you the Qur'an will surely return you to a place of return﴾. It is said: "faradha 'alayka" means "awjaba 'alayka" (He made it obligatory upon you) to act by it.

And His saying: ﴿will surely return you to a place of return﴾. Most of the scholars hold that what is meant by it is Makkah. They said: this verse was revealed to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) while he was at al-Juhfah, and al-Juhfah is a station among the stations between Makkah and Madinah.

The verse is therefore neither Makkan nor Madinan. In some tafsirs it is mentioned: "When the Prophet (ﷺ) emigrated from Makkah to Madinah, he traveled off the main road out of fear of pursuit. Then, when he felt secure, he returned to the road and arrived at al-Juhfah, and he saw the road leading to Makkah and longed for it. Jibril (peace be upon him) came and said: 'Your Lord says: Do you yearn for Makkah and long for it?' He said: 'Yes, it is my land and my birthplace.' He said: 'Your Lord says: ﴿Indeed, He who has imposed upon you the Qur'an will surely return you to a place of return﴾,' meaning: will return you to Makkah victorious over its people."

There is another view regarding the verse, namely that the meaning of His saying ﴿will surely return you to a place of return﴾ is: to the Day of Resurrection. It is also said: to Paradise.

It is narrated from 'Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) that he would praise Jabir ibn 'Abdullah and mention him with goodness. When he was asked about that, he said: "He will be gathered with me." His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, He who has imposed upon you the Qur'an will surely return you to a place of return﴾.

His saying: ﴿Say: My Lord knows best who has come with guidance﴾, meaning: He knows who has come with guidance, and I am the one who came with guidance.

His saying: ﴿and who is in manifest error﴾, meaning: and He knows who is in manifest error, namely the disbelievers.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 28, verse 86:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And you did not expect﴾, i.e., you did not hope or anticipate, ﴿that the Book would be cast down to you﴾, i.e., that the Qur'an would be revealed to you.

And His saying: ﴿But it is a mercy from your Lord﴾. This is an exception of a disconnected kind (istithna' munqati', an exception not of the same category as what precedes it), and its meaning is: rather, your Lord has shown you mercy and so bestowed the Qur'an upon you.

And His saying: ﴿So never be a supporter (zahir) of the disbelievers﴾, i.e., a helper to the disbelievers.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 28, verse 87:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And let them not turn you away from the signs of Allah﴾, meaning: let not the disbelievers prevent you from following the way of Allah. Some of them said its meaning is: be firm with the disbelievers, be harsh toward them, and do not be lax, lest they become eager to turn you away from the way of Allah.

His saying: ﴿after they have been sent down to you﴾, meaning: after the verses clarifying the way have been sent down to you.

His saying: ﴿and invite to your Lord﴾, meaning: to the religion of your Lord.

His saying: ﴿and do not be among the polytheists﴾, meaning: remain steadfast upon monotheism.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 28, verse 88:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And do not invoke with Allah another deity. There is no deity except Him﴾ — meaning: there is no deity other than Him.

And His saying: ﴿Everything will perish except His Face﴾. Sufyan al-Thawri said: except that which is intended by it, His Face and His pleasure, from the deed.

It is also said: ﴿except His Face﴾ means: except Him.

And it is narrated from Sufyan ibn 'Uyayna who said: Whatever Allah has described Himself with in the Book, its tafsir (interpretation) is its recitation; there is no tafsir of it other than that. Allah, may He be exalted, has mentioned "the Face" (al-wajh) in eleven places in the Qur'an. We have already explained that it is one of the attributes of Allah, to be believed in as Allah has mentioned it.

They have also cited, for wajh in the sense of direction (al-tawajjuh) and seeking His pleasure, the verse of the poet:

(I seek forgiveness from Allah for a sin you cannot count... the Lord of the servants, to Him is the face (wajh) and the deed.)

That is, the direction (al-tawajjuh).

And His saying: ﴿And to Him belongs the judgment﴾ — meaning: the decisive judgment.

His judgment is that He sends a people to Paradise and a people to the Fire. And among His judgments also is that He whitens the faces of some people, blackens the faces of some people, makes the scales of some people heavy, and makes the scales of some people light, and similar things. This is in the Hereafter. As for the world, it is the execution of decrees and rulings according to what He knows and wills.

And His saying: ﴿And to Him you will be returned﴾ — meaning: in the Hereafter.
